title: How to photograph a white building
excerpt: Hazy mornings, soft shadows and a little underexposure. What I've learned from twelve years of white concrete.
content:
White buildings are the hardest to photograph well. Here's what works.

Wait for haze

Bright sun burns white walls out. A hazy morning keeps the shadows soft.

Expose for the white

Keep the brightest wall just short of pure white, so it still has texture.

Look for one shadow

A single strong shadow tells you the shape of the whole building.

title: Briefing an architectural photographer: a checklist
excerpt: Drawings, a deadline and where the photos will be used. What helps me most before a shoot.
content:
A good brief saves a day on site. Here's what to send.

The drawings

Plans and a section help me find the best views before I arrive.

Where the photos will go

An award entry needs different photos from a website.

Your favourite corner

Tell me the detail you're proudest of. I'll make sure it's in.

title: Why I put people in my photos
excerpt: Empty buildings look like models. People show the scale, the use and the life of a place.
content:
For years architecture was photographed empty. I think that's changing.

Scale

A person in the frame tells you how big a room really is.

Use

People show what a building is for, better than any caption.

Permission

Everyone recognisable signs a release, or I leave them out.

title: A week of light in Porto
excerpt: Seven days, one stair and a lot of waiting. Notes from the Casa Moreira shoot.
content:
Casa Moreira took one afternoon to shoot and a week to understand.

Monday to Thursday

Rain. I walked the house and learned where the sun would come in.

Friday

Sun at last, through the skylight and down the stair.

The edit

Two hundred photos, four that went into the awards.
